result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers define compact token sets and map all six patterns, with clear rules on which properties may animate and what stays instant. B has the stronger per-pattern reduced-motion table, but it adds a lot beyond motion (toast timing, optimistic updates, error handling) and never says the numbers are starting points to tune. A is tighter, references tokens in its recipe table, and says outright that the values are a proposal to adjust, though its reduced-motion section zeroes the `fast` token while also allowing a `fast` fade. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers set up a small token system and map every pattern to it in a lookup table. A gives the best reduced-motion behaviour for each pattern, but it adds a lot beyond motion, such as toast timing, loading thresholds and optimistic updates, and it never says the numbers are starting points to tune. B is tighter and maps patterns straight to token names. It also explicitly frames the values as a starting proposal to try and adjust. Its reduced-motion section is less complete for each pattern and partly contradicts its own rule that durations drop to zero.
